data.one_liner: Translate Flutter applications using standard gettext .po files with positional and named arguments.
data.what_it_does: Allows loading standard .po translation files as assets in a Flutter application. Provides translation extension methods with support for plurals, contexts, comments, and both positional and named arguments.
use_when: You prefer standard gettext (.po) files for managing application translations.
You need pluralization and positional or named arguments within translated strings.
You want to avoid code-generation steps for localization files.
avoid_when: You prefer type-safe generated keys as provided by packages like slang.
Your project relies heavily on the standard Flutter intl and ARB translation pipeline.
strengths: Supports .po translation files compatible with standard gettext translation tools.
Supports positional arguments, named arguments, and plurals out of the box.
weaknesses: Translation keys are plain strings rather than type-safe generated properties.
Dependent on asset loading for .po files.
data.setup_notes: Add the package and flutter_localizations, configure assets/i18n/ in pubspec.yaml, and add GettextLocalizationsDelegate to localizationsDelegates.

alternatives.name: intl
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want standard official Flutter localization support using ARB files.

alternatives.name: slang
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want a strongly typed localization system with code generation.

alternatives.name: easy_localization
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want easy translation loading from JSON, CSV, or YAML files without code generation.

data.minimal_example: Text(context.translate('There is {0} apple', keyPlural: 'There are {0} apples', pArgs: [1]));
